ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there are three circles mutually internally tangent/intersecting at point L, with centers G, J, and K respectively. Points H, F, and L are marked on the large circle, and segment GH goes from center G to H on the circle. The middle circle has center J; in the figure it can be seen that it passes through G and L, and G, J, L are on the same straight line. The small circle has center K; in the figure it can be seen that it passes through J and L, and J, K, L are on the same straight line. Reasoning: Because H and L are both on the large circle with center G, GH and GL are both radii of the large circle. Given GH=10, therefore GL=10. The middle circle has center J and passes through G, L, and G, J, L are collinear, so J is the midpoint of GL, hence JL=10/2=5. The small circle has center K and passes through J, L, and J, K, L are collinear, so K is the midpoint of JL, hence JK=JL/2=5/2=2.5.

raw_record.question_text: Circles $G$, $J$, and $K$ all intersect at $L$. If $GH=10$, find $JK$.

method.method_draft: Read the diagram as three circles named by their centers: large circle centered at G, middle circle centered at J, and small circle centered at K. From the image, H and L lie on circle G, so GH and GL are radii of the large circle. The text gives GH = 10, hence GL = 10. The diagram also shows the middle circle centered at J passing through both G and L, with G, J, L collinear; therefore J is the midpoint of GL and JL = 5. The small circle centered at K passes through both J and L, with J, K, L collinear; therefore K is the midpoint of JL and JK = JL/2 = 2.5.

method.method_draft: Set up a one-dimensional coordinate model along the line through G, J, K, and L as shown. Put G at coordinate 0. Since H and L are on circle G and GH = 10, GL is a radius, so place L at coordinate 10. The middle circle is centered at J and passes through both G and L, so J must be halfway between 0 and 10, at coordinate 5. The small circle is centered at K and passes through both J and L, so K must be halfway between 5 and 10, at coordinate 7.5. Therefore JK = 7.5 - 5 = 2.5.
